assessment: Major:5 demonstrated core issue groups;5 Minor groups;1 qualified sign concern
inspection_outcome: Core normal-form,frame,cubical,DGA and all-object projective OS construction fail as printed; explicit bounded repairs; intended final Koszulness not refuted.

findings.title: The inclusion invariant in Lemma3.20 is not compatible with structural composition
findings.classification: Major: demonstrated invalid core normal-form derivation; conclusion locally repairable
findings.statement: Page27 defines iota(S) on all non-bottom local-interval elements by raw inclusion and iota(f)=f^{-1}, extends by composition, and uses this as a well-defined invariant to recover normal forms.
findings.witness: Let L=B3 on a,b,c and G={a,b,c,abc}. The outer S={a,abc} has upper interval[a,abc] with induced building set{ab,ac,abc}. Refine the upper interval by T={ab,abc}, leaving the lower factor unchanged. Comp_a(ab)=b, so the composite nested set is U={a,b,abc}. All building/nested/irreducibility hypotheses hold.
findings.calculation: The iterated source has middle factor[a,ab], whereas the direct source has[0,b]. Phi is represented by j:[0,b]->[a,ab], j(x)=a∨x. Thus iota(Phi)=j^{-1} sends ab to b. The staged raw inclusions send the same ab to ab. The two expressions for the same categorical composite have different proposed invariant values.
findings.alternative_reading: For the maximal building set Comp equals inclusion, so the defect is invisible there. The paper allows general building sets and the Boolean top-containing set above. Ignoring Phi would change the defined composition and is not a valid reading.
repair: Use the building set of each object, with tagged disjoint union under tensor, as the underlying set. On a structural block use c_S(Y)=Comp_{τ_S(G)}(Y), defined on its induced building set. On an isomorphism use the inverse poset map restricted to building sets.

Lemma3.13's earlier pointwise identity says that successive Comp maps equal the composite Comp after Phi^{-1}. Naturality follows from preservation of the maximal defining fiber under lattice isomorphisms. Reordering permutes blocks; units use Comp_0=Id; tensor maps are disjoint unions. These check every defining compatibility, including the composition omitted by the old argument.

Images of labelled source-factor tops recover S and the node assignment. To recover the forward interval isomorphism h_i, use h_i(g)=τ_S(H_i)∨c_F(g), not just restriction of c_F. Since every atom is in the source building set and a finite atomic lattice is join-generated by its atoms, h_i is determined on the whole lattice.
The argument uses only pre-3.20 factor/Comp/Phi lemmas and is noncircular. Existence follows from the defining relations, and the corrected invariant proves uniqueness.
findings.impact: The printed proof of Lemma3.20 is invalid, affecting its uses in the presentation, shuffle/free comparison and cubical discussion until corrected. This example does not refute the normal-form conclusion or final Koszulness.
findings.cross_check: Independent native helper /root/check_0171_applications read the relevant definitions and pages18–35 and supplied the same general repair. Its notes.md SHA256 is 0bd5228a2c7aa46b395bd0d4bafe58cb98c3110762fd8b6729d5076369146a31; those notes were read in full (297 lines).

findings.title: The normal-frame theorem excludes a necessary rank-one top interval
findings.classification: Major: false core normal-monomial statement as printed; complete local boundary repair
findings.statement: Proposition5.23 and Lemma5.24 demand a spanning frame with no rank1 local intervals, but the proposed frame is {nodes with local rank>1} union {top}.
findings.witness: For a rank1 irreducible built lattice, the unique FY class and one-vertex free-operad monomial exist, yet there is no spanning nested set without a rank1 interval. In B3 with maximal building set and atom order a<b<c, S={ab,abc} is a quadratic normal monomial: its lower node has rank2, whereas all leading quadratic terms have a nonminimal atom as lower node. Its top local interval[ab,abc] has rank1.
findings.calculation: Any rank3 frame having every local rank at least2 can have only the top node by rank additivity. Such a frame yields only EL clusters. It cannot produce S={ab,abc}, whose non-top interval has rank2. Exact enumeration gives6 normal B3 monomials, while the printed frames yield3.
repair: Replace the phrase by 'no rank1 local intervals except possibly the top interval' in both statements.

Keep the printed frame formula. Removed non-top rank1 nodes form clusters in the frame intervals. A proper retained node had residual rank>1, so its cluster is proper and k_G<rank(local)-1. The retained top may have residual rank1, for which k_top=rank(local)-1 is permitted.

The already printed special bound for k_top handles a rank1 top frame interval by k_top=0. The exponent formula alpha_G=rank(local)-k_G-1 then gives positive proper-node exponents and a possibly zero top exponent, exactly matching the spanning version of the FY normal basis.
Uniqueness follows from the intrinsic criterion defining the frame and the unique decomposition into its local clusters. The EL-normal-cluster argument survives with F7's weaker fiber-minimum step.
findings.impact: The printed normal-monomial parametrization and its basis-count proof are false at this boundary. The correction restores the missing classes and supports the intended Groebner conclusion; no counterexample to that conclusion is claimed.

findings.title: The displayed cubical reordering formula can produce a node in no current factor
findings.classification: Major: core action formula is not defined in a permitted example; categorical replacement available
findings.statement: Page57 sets G_i^sigma=G_sigma(i) joined with earlier selected nodes strictly below G_sigma(i). That added join is already below G_sigma(i), so the formula leaves the original node unchanged.
findings.witness: Use B3,G={a,b,c,abc} and spanning nested antichain S={a,b,abc}. In an ordering that first inserts a, the current factors are[0,a] and[a,abc]. The next original node b belongs to neither factor.
findings.calculation: The printed formula gives b because the earlier node a is incomparable with b. The required induced node is ab in[a,abc], whose Comp image is b. Hence the claimed tensor generator for the printed b cannot be formed.
repair: Start with T={top}. For each next original node G in the chosen ordering, let P be the unique least element of T strictly above G. Put A=τ_T(P) and insert H=A∨G in the factor[A,P]. Then update T by adjoining G.

Lemma3.16/product-factorization gives A<H<P, H in the induced building set, and Comp_A(H)=G. Thus the insertion is permitted and adds exactly the required original node. The antichain example gives H=a∨b=ab.

With the corrected normal form in F1, every chain class determines its original-node ordering and this insertion reconstructs it, up to the already quotiented source isomorphisms. The symmetric group acts by permuting orderings. It is free, preserves the composite, has the prescribed degree-n orbit fibers, and is compatible with concatenation.
The same description respects induced atom orders in the shuffle category. The degree-n composition target in Definition6.1 should be written Hom_n(A,B).
findings.impact: The printed explicit proof of Proposition6.3 needs this replacement. It does not exhibit a noncubical category. Exact checks covered29 orderings of all spanning nested sets for the two stated Boolean B3 building sets.

findings.title: The projective Leray quotient does not carry the differential printed in Definition6.4
findings.classification: Major: ill-defined DGA in a core Koszul comparison; bounded DGA correction established
findings.statement: Definition6.4 kills e_top but then sets d(e_G)=x_G for every G, including top. A differential on the quotient would have to send the zero class e_top to zero.
findings.witness: Take L=B2 and maximal building set G={a,b,t}. It is an irreducible built geometric lattice. The pure-x quotient is Q[x_a,x_b,x_t]/(x_a+x_t,x_b+x_t,x_a x_b), isomorphic to Q[t]/(t^2).
findings.calculation: x_t is nonzero: send x_a,x_b to -t and x_t to t in Q[t]/(t^2), and send every e-generator to0. All defining algebra relations of B vanish under this map. But d([e_t])=[x_t] is nonzero although [e_t]=0. Exact Groebner reduction leaves x_t and kills x_t^2.
findings.alternative_reading: The displayed formula could have been intended only for proper G, but that exception is absent. Interpreting the ideal as a differential ideal would additionally kill x_top and change the FY piece, so it does not reproduce the stated bar model.
repair: Omit e_top from the projective generator list, or explicitly set d(e_top)=0 before quotienting. Define d(e_G)=x_G only for G proper and d(x_G)=0.

The nonnested support ideal is stable because replacing an e_G by x_G preserves its support. The atom-sum relations are closed, and d^2=0 on generators; thus the corrected graded derivation is well-defined.

Projective OS differences map to sum_{G>=H,G<top}e_G - sum_{G>=H',G<top}e_G. Their differentials are (-x_top)-(-x_top)=0 by the atom sums. This verifies the closed-generator boundary of the intended projective map.
For the affine model, retain e_top and d(e_top)=x_top. Then atom sums make the affine e_H images closed. Killing only e_top is not a DGA quotient with that affine differential.
findings.impact: The isomorphism of complexes and quasi-isomorphism invoked for Corollary6.6 cannot be justified with the printed DGA. The local corrected DGA exists, but a full independent verification of the external Leray quasi-isomorphism, cooperad compatibility and every suspension convention is not claimed. Corollary6.10's separate Groebner route is not refuted by this example.

additional_general_repair_and_limits.claim: Proper building elements index the odd structural generators and the projective bar differential.
reasoning: Page 58 explicitly defines [G]^odd only for G different from the maximal element. The odd category on page 57 introduces the permutation-sign quotient on chains.

The projective Orlik-Solomon cooperad is the projective algebra shifted by [-1], with its unit in grading 1. The structure map includes delta in one factor, and the source remains the projective subalgebra.
The cobar formula on page 60 explicitly sums over proper G in each factor. The bar formula contracts a degree-one structural generator and uses the corresponding permutation signature.
Consequently a projective bar model has no independent edge generator corresponding to cutting at the global top. This agrees with using exterior generators for proper G only.
The bounded check does not re-prove every odd-cooperad sign relation or all global regradings. The shift convention is preserved rather than silently replaced by an unshifted cooperad.
additional_general_repair_and_limits.status: Relevant indexing and differential mechanism checked.

additional_general_repair_and_limits.claim: The relation e_top=0 is not stable under the differential printed in Definition 6.4.
reasoning: The source first takes all e_G and all x_G for G in the building set, and adds e_top to the ideal. Page 62 then gives d(e_G)=x_G without excluding top.
A derivation on the free algebra descends to its quotient only if the defining ideal is stable. Here the image of the generator e_top of the ideal is x_top.
COUNTEREXAMPLE01 proves x_top is nonzero in an allowed irreducible built lattice. Thus the problem is a literal failure of well-definedness, not an unverified suspicion or an OCR ambiguity.
additional_general_repair_and_limits.status: Confirmed by actual images and an explicit finite example.

additional_general_repair_and_limits.claim: The proper-exterior-generator correction defines a DGA.
additional_general_repair_and_limits.corrected_definition: B_pr=(Lambda_Q(e_G : G in G\{top}) tensor Q[x_G : G in G])/J, where J is generated by e_S x_T with S union T nonnested, and by sum_{G>=H}x_G for every atom H. Use bidegrees |e_G|=(0,1), |x_G|=(2,0), d of bidegree (2,-1), d e_G=x_G and d x_G=0.
proof: Use graded commutativity for total degree: each e is odd and each x is even. Thus the e generators form an exterior algebra over Q.

For a mixed nonnested generator e_S x_T, applying d replaces one proper e_G by x_G. Every surviving summand has exactly the same underlying support S union T, so it is again a nonnested-ideal element. This remains true if a G was already in T, in which case its x exponent increases.
The atom-linear generators have zero differential because every x is closed.
Hence d(J) is contained in J. Since d^2 is zero on all free generators, the odd derivation has d^2=0 on the free graded algebra and the quotient.
All x variables, especially x_top, are retained. No relation x_top=0 is added.

additional_general_repair_and_limits.claim: The corrected model is a sub-DGA of the affine model, not the indicated differential quotient.
proof: Let hatB have all e_G, including z=e_top, with the mixed nonnested and atom-linear relations but without e_top=0. The same support argument makes it a DGA, now with d z=x_top.

Adding top to a set neither creates nor removes a nonnested antichain: top is comparable with every building element. Therefore the defining ideal of hatB is the extension of J, and as graded algebras hatB=B_pr tensor Lambda(z).
The algebra B_pr embeds in hatB and is stable under d. The graded projection q:hatB->B_pr with q(z)=0 exists, but it is not a chain map when x_top is nonzero.

A minimal correction to the manuscript can either write B_pr directly with proper e variables, or regard the e_top=0 quotient only as an underlying graded-algebra presentation and define d on its remaining proper generators. It must not retain the universal formula on the zero class e_top.

additional_general_repair_and_limits.claim: The projective comparison remains a chain map; the affine atomic generators must not be confused with projective elements.
additional_general_repair_and_limits.assumptions: For the general OS quotient, use the well-defined underlying affine algebra map asserted in the manuscript, phi_aff(e_H)=sum_{G>=H}e_G. The full external proof that this respects all circuit relations is not reconstructed here.
proof: Write eta_H=sum_{G>=H,G!=top} e_G. The atom-linear relation gives d eta_H=-x_top, independently of H.

Let phi_pr=q phi_aff as a graded algebra map, where q is the graded projection of L04. On exterior representatives, the graded Leibniz rule gives d phi_pr(alpha)=-x_top phi_pr(delta alpha), with delta(e_H)=1.
Therefore the restriction to the projective algebra overline{OS}=ker(delta) has zero differential and is a chain map into B_pr.

An individual affine generator e_H is not in ker(delta); its image eta_H is generally not closed. Requiring each eta_H to be closed would incorrectly test an affine map instead of the projective comparison actually used on page 62.

Equivalently, writing every affine image with z on the left gives phi_aff(alpha)=phi_pr(alpha)+z phi_pr(delta alpha). Thus a projective element has no z coefficient and its affine image already lies in the sub-DGA B_pr.
additional_general_repair_and_limits.status: Chain compatibility proved; general OS-algebra well-definedness is an explicitly retained input.

additional_general_repair_and_limits.claim: A conditional objectwise quasi-isomorphism reduction preserves the distinction from the external Leray theorem.
proof: Assume the lattice has positive rank and choose an atom H0. Put eta=eta_{H0} and v=z+eta. Then d v=x_top-x_top=0.
Changing the odd variable z to v gives an isomorphism of DGAs hatB=B_pr tensor Lambda(v), with d v=0. This uses only d eta=-x_top and graded commutativity.

On the Orlik-Solomon side, delta(e_{H0})=1 and delta^2=0 give OS=overline{OS} tensor Lambda(e_{H0}): every alpha decomposes uniquely as (alpha-e_{H0}delta alpha)+e_{H0}delta alpha, with both coefficients in ker(delta).
Under these decompositions, phi_aff sends e_{H0} to v and sends the projective factor through phi_pr. Thus phi_aff=phi_pr tensor id.
Over Q, taking cohomology commutes with tensoring with the two-dimensional zero-differential exterior algebra. Therefore phi_aff is an objectwise quasi-isomorphism if and only if phi_pr is.

In rank one, the proper exterior set is empty and the atom-linear relation gives x_top=0; the formula reduces to Q and its one-generator exterior extension. A zero-rank unit object, if separately adjoined, is treated directly rather than by choosing a nonexistent atom.
additional_general_repair_and_limits.limit: This proves an implication conditional on the affine comparison. It does not prove that the cited affine Leray map is a quasi-isomorphism for all built lattices, and the atom choice is not claimed to give a natural splitting of odd cooperads.
additional_general_repair_and_limits.status: Conditional algebraic reduction complete; external quasi-isomorphism not re-proved.

additional_general_repair_and_limits.claim: Compatibility with the local bar differential and what remains imported for Corollary 6.6.
reasoning: Page 39 defines FYPD([G]) for proper G by inserting a factor x_G and transporting the remaining variables through the Comp_G rule. Pages 39-40 give the relation checks.

A proper exterior monomial e_{G1}...e_{Gr} has differential sum_i (-1)^{i-1} e_{G1}...omit(e_{Gi})...e_{Gr} x_{Gi}. Its sign is the sign of moving the contracted generator to the position used by the bar differential.

Thus, once the graded nested-set component identification quoted from [5], Proposition 5.1.4, is used, the local contraction operation is precisely the insertion of x_G in FYPD([G]). There is no top contraction in the projective case.

The corrected B_pr has exactly the same underlying bigraded algebra as the manuscript's graded quotient by e_top. Therefore the cited graded vector-space decomposition indexed by spanning S with |S|=d+1 has not been changed by the correction.

The complete graded decomposition, its global odd-cooperad compatibility, the identification of the comparison with the canonical quadratic-dual map, and the external Leray quasi-isomorphism remain inputs for the full Corollary 6.6 argument.

The correction supplies the missing well-defined differential and is consistent with those required local operations. This bounded check does not claim a new proof of all those external and categorical identifications.
additional_general_repair_and_limits.status: Local differential compatibility checked; full comparison dependencies explicitly retained.

additional_U23_witness.object: The geometric lattice of flats of U_{2,3}: bottom 0, atoms a,b,c, and top t. Use the maximal building set G={a,b,c,t}. This is an allowed irreducible built lattice, and U_{2,3} is connected as a matroid as well.
additional_U23_witness.nested_sets: A nested set contains at most one atom; t may always be added.
quotient_calculation: The atom-linear relations are x_a+x_t=x_b+x_t=x_c+x_t=0. Set h=x_t, so each atom variable is -h.
A pair of distinct atoms is nonnested, giving x_a x_b=0 and hence h^2=0. The mixed relations e_i x_j=0 for i!=j imply e_i h=0. The exterior relations give e_i e_j=0 for distinct atoms.
The resulting graded quotient by e_t has Q-basis 1,e_a,e_b,e_c,h. In particular h is nonzero.

An explicit witness for h nonzero is the quotient-algebra homomorphism to Q[h]/(h^2) sending all e's to zero, x_t to h, and every atom x_i to -h. It respects every defining relation and has nonzero image of x_t.
The relation e_t=0 is sent by the prescribed free derivation to h!=0. Therefore d does not descend.
additional_U23_witness.exact_tool_check: The atom-linear relation matrix in columns (x_a,x_b,x_c,x_t) has rational rank 3; adjoining the row x_t=0 increases rank to 4. The reviewer-authored Fraction row-reduction in independent_checks.json verifies this.
corrected_cohomology: In B_pr, d e_a=d e_b=d e_c=-h. The only nonzero differential has matrix [-1,-1,-1], of rank 1.
H^0=Q, H^1 has basis e_b-e_a and e_c-e_a, and H^2=0. This agrees with the projective Orlik-Solomon degree-one dimension 2 of U_{2,3}.

For the affine extension, adjoining z with d z=h gives differential ranks 1 and 1 in consecutive degrees and cohomology dimensions (1,3,2,0), matching the expected affine dimensions in this example. This is a finite check, not a proof of the general Leray theorem.

additional_U23_witness.target: The alternative repair of also imposing x_top=0
reasoning: To turn the original quotient into a differential quotient by closing the ideal under d, one would add x_t=0.
In COUNTEREXAMPLE01, this also forces all x_i=0. The resulting algebra has basis 1,e_a,e_b,e_c and zero differential.
Its H^1 has dimension 3, while the projective Orlik-Solomon algebra has degree-one dimension 2. Thus this alternative repair does not preserve the intended projective comparison.
The valid proper-exterior correction retains x_t, even though x_t is exact in B_pr.
additional_U23_witness.status: Explicit counterevidence against an overbroad repair.

findings.title: Proposition2.23 and the following top-degree statement

evidence.anchor: Proposition2.23 and the following top-degree statement
evidence.witness: B2 with reducible building set{a,b} is allowed. Def2.22 gives FY=Z[x_a,x_b]/(x_a,x_b)=Z. The displayed projective quotient gives Z[x_a,x_b]/(x_a-x_b)=Z[t], since every subset is nested. It is not isomorphic to FY. The claimed universal top degree2(rank-1) and x_top generator also fail because top is not in the building set.
evidence.repair: Restrict the projective presentation/top generator statement to irreducible built lattices. For a product with m maximal building factors, the top degree is2(rank(L)-m), obtained by tensoring the factor rings. Later Gen/Prop4.4 and FYPD arity definitions explicitly use irreducibles.

findings.impact: Irreducible arity qualification preserves later FY usage.

findings.title: Odd projective OS object assignment on p58

evidence.anchor: Odd projective OS object assignment on p58
evidence.witness: The literal assignment OSproj(L)[-1] for every built lattice is not strong monoidal. A rank1 factor has one basis element in shifted degree1, so two factors tensor to one element in degree2. Their product lattice B2 has projective OS dimensions1,1 in original degrees0,1, hence shifted degrees1,2 and total dimension2. The rank-zero unit is also sent to degree1 rather than the tensor unit.
evidence.repair: Define the displayed value on irreducible arities only, then extend on arbitrary tensor products by the tensor of those arity values and send the empty product to the tensor unit. This fixes the object-level dimension obstruction. It does not, by itself, settle the separate shifted braiding/sign convention.

findings.impact: Literal core projective OS assignment cannot be strong monoidal; irreducible-only values plus tensor extension repair object-level obstruction, not all signs.

findings.title: The general FY(S) formula needs a weak inequality
findings.classification: Minor: local displayed formula; elementary definition remains valid
findings.witness: For G=top the set is empty. If G is itself a proper node of S, the printed choice is its parent, whose lower endpoint already contains G; the resulting generator index is the bottom, which is not in the local building set. For B3 maximal G and S={ab,abc}, input h_ab should go into[0,ab], not the bottom of[ab,abc].
findings.repair: Use G'=min S_{>=G}. Spanning gives existence, the nested forest gives uniqueness, and minimality ensures τ_S(G')∨G is above the local bottom. This agrees with each elementary FY[G] and with the identity S={top}.
findings.impact: No defect is inferred in the independently checked elementary maps or their relations.

findings.title: Lemma5.25 asserts equality of two fibers when only their minima agree
findings.classification: Minor: unnecessary auxiliary equality; the proof is repaired by a direct minimum argument
findings.witness: Let M=U_{2,3} on a,b,c direct-sum U_{1,1} on d, with maximal building set and atom order a<b<c<d. The normal EL cluster S={a,line(abc),top} has all local ranks1. Choose G1=a, G2=line(abc), A=τ_{S\{G1}}(G2)=0, and H_G2=b.
findings.calculation: The left fiber {H:A∨H=A∨b} is {b}; the displayed right fiber {H:τ_S(G2)∨H=G2} is {b,c}. They are unequal, while both minima are b.
findings.repair: In general put v=τ_S(G2), u=τ_{S\{G1}}(G2), and h=H_G2. If u∨H=u∨h, then v∨H=v∨h=G2, so the left fiber lies in the right fiber. It contains h, which is the minimum of the right fiber by definition. Therefore the minima coincide, which is all inequality(24) needs. The first fiber equality is justified separately by the nested-factor product decomposition.
findings.impact: The increasing-label conclusion and subsequent normal-cluster argument survive. No counterexample to Lemma5.25's conclusion is claimed.

findings.title: The outlook rank and building-decomposition axioms omit necessary qualifications
findings.classification: Minor/local outlook corrections; not used by the geometric-lattice Koszul results

parts.witness: On E={a,b}, set r(empty)=0, r(a)=r(b)=1, r(ab)=0. All printed submodular inequalities and r(A∪{x})<=r(A)+1 hold, but monotonicity fails. This is not a matroid rank function.
parts.repair: Add r(A)<=r(B) for A⊂B, or require 0<=r(A∪{x})-r(A)<=1. Together with the other printed axioms this gives the standard finite matroid rank conditions.

parts.witness: For the genuine simple loopless matroid U2,3, let nu be discrete on proper subsets and one-block on the full ground set. Let nu' be one-block on every nonempty subset. Both satisfy refinement, idempotence on blocks and rank additivity. They agree on all flats (empty, singletons and E), hence yield the same building set{a,b,c,E}, but differ on each pair. The claimed data equivalence is therefore not injective.
parts.repair: If an actual bijection is intended, require closure compatibility nu(X)=nu(cl(X)) restricted to X. For a flat, rank-additive blocks give a direct-sum restriction, hence closed component factors; refinement identifies the maximal trivial-block flats. Conversely a building set supplies those factor partitions, and closure compatibility determines the nonflat subsets. Alternatively state that the proposed decompositions are a richer structure rather than equivalent data.

findings.impact: The proposed extension cannot be taken as a proved equivalent axiomatization in its present form. The paper's earlier results assume geometric lattices and do not use these outlook definitions.

findings.title: The lower branch of the polymatroid FY map has the wrong generator index
findings.classification: Minor: explicit index correction, already testable in the matroid special case
findings.statement: The displayed map sends h_G' to 1⊗h_G in the branch G'<=G.
findings.witness: Take B3 with maximal building set, cut G=ab and G'=a. The source relation is h_a=0, but the printed image is1⊗h_ab. In the lower B2 interval FY=Q[t]/(t^2), h_ab=t is nonzero.
findings.repair: Replace h_G by h_G' in that branch. This agrees with the earlier elementary FY map and kills the source atom relation in this example.
findings.impact: The displayed formula is not well-defined as written. No general certification or refutation of the proposed polymatroid extension is made from this local index correction.

qualified_observations.topic: Shifted odd OS signs on pp58–59
qualified_observations.detail: Under the standard Koszul braiding and the pointwise displayed maps, B3 with G={a,b,c,top} and alpha=delta(e_c e_b e_a) gives first a then ab=-1⊗1⊗1. First b then ab gives+1⊗1⊗1 before the final swap; swapping two shifted degree1 units gives-1⊗1⊗1, so the composites agree rather than being negatives. Page16 explicitly says that graded commutative means with Koszul signs. The odd-OS target is called graded abelian groups, without a separately specified alternative symmetry. A second native helper independently confirmed the calculation and that ordinary coherent suspension transport does not remove this discrepancy. An ordinary ungraded flip makes the required negative relation hold in this example, but is not a verified repair of the whole structure. This note retains the exact failure under the standard Koszul symmetry as a qualified construction/convention concern for parent integration, without claiming a false final theorem or an unconditional convention-independent counterexample.
qualified_observations.conditional_on: Standard Koszul symmetry for the displayed shifted maps

focused_independent_acceptance.performer: Current acceptance primary /root; native read-only auxiliaries separately attributed

per_problem.reasoning: In B3 with building set {a,b,c,t}, both the building-set product condition and nestedness of {a,t} and its refinement {ab,t} in [a,t] hold. Comp_a(ab)=b. The structural-composition identification sends the ab-labelled iterated factor to b, whereas the raw non-bottom inclusion invariant sends it to ab. It therefore fails the defining composition relation, not merely a choice of order. Replacing the domain by tagged building elements and inclusion by Comp fixes the example. The pointwise Comp/Phi identity is proved earlier in Lemma 3.13 by maximality; it supplies a noncircular compatibility argument. Source-factor tops recover the nested nodes; joining the local bottom with the recovered Comp image recovers interval maps on building elements, hence on atoms and the entire atomic lattice. This invalidates the printed uniqueness proof but does not disprove the corrected normal-form theorem.

per_problem.decision: Confirmed Major local combinatorial statement/proof defect
per_problem.reasoning: The rank-one irreducible arity already contradicts the universal exclusion of rank-one frame intervals. In maximal-built B3, a frame {ab,t} has proper local rank two and top local rank one. The printed exclusion loses three of the six FY normal monomials; the top exception recovers the Hilbert count 1+4z+z^2. The exponent bijection alpha_G=rank(local interval)-k_G-1 requires positive proper-frame exponents and permits zero at top. The repair is to forbid only non-top rank-one intervals. The formula fr(S)={local rank>1} union {top} in the source is direct counterevidence to interpreting the exclusion as intentional. This repairs the enumerative proof step; no false final Groebner/Koszul conclusion is established.

The printed join only uses earlier nodes strictly below G and thus remains G. In allowed B3 with building set {a,b,c,t}, inserting a first produces [0,a] and [a,t]; the next node b lies in neither current factor. The required current upper generator is ab. For each subsequent node G, take its minimal containing current node P, A=tau_T(P), and insert A join G in [A,P]; nestedness ensures A < A join G < P and Comp_A(A join G)=G.
